features.feature_value: Kept non-hateful/opinionated content, focused removals on overt sexism/hate/name-calling/president-targeting and anything dangerous to others.
features.evidence_span: only take down posts that were overtly sexist, hateful, name calling the president
features.rationale: The participant explicitly states a removal threshold around sexism/hate/name-calling and allowing opinions when not hateful/dangerous.

features.feature_value: Used language quality and factuality cues; removed abusive/foul language but allowed harsh yet substance-addressing comments.
features.evidence_span: focused mainly on the use of language and facts... anyone with abusive and foul language are deleted... allow comments that really addressed the American problems even if they sounded harsh.
features.rationale: They describe specific cue-driven criteria (abuse/foul language vs addressing problems) affecting keep/remove.

features.feature_value: Compared how each post behaved (dirty/takedown/putting down); in cases of unfair aggression/misrepresentation, rejected both viewpoints.
features.evidence_span: throwing dirt... In those cases, I rejected both viewpoints.
features.rationale: They explain influence through comparing aggression across the pair and sometimes rejecting both.

features.feature_value: Tried to approve posts that represent views without becoming overly personal; removal when crossing a line.
features.evidence_span: approve the ones that both represented their views without getting into too personal of an attack... some of it is just blatantly crossing a line.
features.rationale: The participant gives a boundary between acceptable political critique and impermissible personal attacks.

features.feature_value: Affirmed free speech but removed content that is hateful/distasteful; criticized using curse words instead of thoughtful wording.
features.evidence_span: We all have the right of free speech, but... hateful and distasteful should not be allowed... Using curse works instead of taking the time to think of another word
features.rationale: They explicitly articulate what speech is allowed vs prohibited (hateful/distasteful; cursing).

features.feature_value: Claimed the difference between sides/pair didn’t matter; leaned toward allowing because nothing ‘crossed the line,’ emphasizing free speech and abuse tolerance.
features.evidence_span: The difference in each side didn't really matter to me... nothing crossed the line... Love it or hate it freedom of speech is the American way
features.rationale: They downplay pair comparison impact and anchor decisions to an explicit ‘crossed the line’ standard tied to free-speech framing.

features.feature_value: Did not keep either because at least one post made no sense / lacked coherence.
features.evidence_span: other post I didn't agree with because of what they making absolutely no sense, I chose to not to keep either
features.rationale: Their decision is driven by intelligibility/understandability rather than ideology, leading to rejecting both.

features.feature_value: In some examples, even if one expressed legitimate viewpoints, the paired behavior led to rejecting both viewpoints.
features.evidence_span: one might express legitimate viewpoints while the other was putting down the other side. In those cases, I rejected both viewpoints.
features.rationale: They describe a symmetric rejection strategy driven by perceived unfair treatment across the pair.
